articles.title: ORLEN Cites Foreign Operations as Profit Rises
articles.description: Poland's majority state-owned ORLEN reported a 40 percent increase in revenue from foreign markets, saying expansion abroad has allowed it to pursue profitability while holding down its prices at home.

articles.title: Uniper to Increase Dividend
articles.description: Uniper plans a dividend of EUR 0.77 per share for 2026, up seven percent year-on-year, as net profit adjusted for nonrecurring items more than doubled for the first nine months of 2026.

articles.title: Türkiye reveals two new oil fields as COP31 opens in Antalya
articles.description: Türkiye has announced two additional oil discoveries in its southeastern Gabar region, with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan disclosing the finds as the COP31 climate conference got underway in Antalya.

articles.title: ADNOC Gas Profit Flat YoY as Hormuz Continues to Weigh on Exports
articles.description: The natural gas processing and sales arm of Abu Dhabi National Oil Co reported $1.34 billion in net profit for Q3, stable compared to the same three-month period in 2025 as high prices offset lower sales volumes.

articles.title: Oil drops further as Trump eases Middle East conflict fears
articles.description: Crude oil benchmarks extended their decline on Tuesday after US President Donald Trump indicated he has no immediate plans to escalate military operations against Iran, tempering weeks of anxiety over Middle East supply disruptions.

articles.title: QatarEnergy to acquire 25% stake in Namibia’s PEL82 licence
articles.description: QatarEnergy has agreed to acquire a 25% participating interest in an offshore oil and gas exploration licence in Namibia from Chevron Namibia Exploration II, a subsidiary of Chevron.

articles.title: US Holds Off Strikes after Qatari Mediation
articles.description: Trump indicated he is keen to pursue diplomacy with Iran and wind down the war following a White House meeting with the prime minister of Qatar, the main mediator between the warring sides.

articles.title: China’s Coal Buyers Resist Waiver Demands in New Indonesian Deals
articles.description: China’s coal importers are resisting attempts by Indonesian exporters to include waiver clauses in the new supply contracts to free them from strict delivery volumes if the Indonesian government decides to restrict export or output quotas again, sources familiar with the negotiations have told Bloomberg. Indonesia, which is the world’s biggest exporter of thermal coal, has changed its production and export policies several times this year, stifling international shipments and forcing China, the world’s top coal consumer, to tweak…

articles.title: Qatar LNG Loadings Gain Pace
articles.description: Liquefied natural gas loadings onto tankers from Qatar have picked up over the past few weeks, suggesting the major exporter is seeking to get more cargoes to the global market despite ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Ukraine Peace Talks Face an Uphill Battle as Winter Approaches
articles.description: After fading into the background when the war with Iran began, the US diplomatic push to end Russia’s invasion of Ukraine is intensifying again, with the first US-Ukraine-Russia talks since February scheduled for November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi. On the eve of the talks, US President Donald Trump said on the CBS program 60 Minutes that he believes “we’re very close to a deal” and that the war is “going to end soon.” Nevertheless, expectations of a breakthrough at the negotiations this week are low. articles.title: Iran War Set to Drive A Drop in Global Fossil Fuel Emissions in 2026
articles.description: Global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026 from a year earlier, due to the oil shock from the Iran war and increased solar and wind power generation, new research by the Global Carbon Project showed on Tuesday. The 2026 Global Carbon Budget projects 38.2 billion tons of fossil carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions this year, down by 0.4% from last year, amid a slump in emissions from oil as a result of the Hormuz trade and energy price shock, the scientists behind the project said. “Emissions…

articles.title: Beetaloo Energy secures RL11 licence for Carpentaria shale gas fairway
articles.description: Beetaloo Energy Australia has secured Retention Licence 11 (RL11) from the Northern Territory Department of Mining and Energy for rights over the Carpentaria unconventional shale gas fairway in Australia’s Northern Territory.

articles.title: Tribunal Hearings Begin in UK-Argentina Row Over Falklands Oil Project
articles.description: The Hamburg-based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea on Tuesday begins hearings of Argentina’s complaint about the UK’s oil drilling project north of the Falkland Islands, which Argentinian President Javier Milei claims is unlawful amid a recently revived row with Britain over who controls the Falklands. The Sea Lion oil field is operated by Navitas Petroleum Development and Production Ltd (NPDP), a UK-based fully owned subsidiary of Israeli Navitas Petroleum, and its British partner Rockhopper Exploration. The…

articles.title: China Is Buying Oil Again After Months of Living Off Its Stockpiles
articles.description: China’s crude oil imports last month hit the highest since March, reaching 41.94 million tons, equal to around 9.88 million barrels daily. The October average was a 9.4% increase on the previous month as well, Reuters reported. Seaborne crude oil imports specifically went up by 12% in October from September, according to data from Kpler. Citing official customs data, the publication also reported that despite the monthly increase and the seven-month high, October’s total in oil imports was still 13.3% below the volume for October 2025.…

articles.title: U.S. Military Coordinates With Saudi Oil Tankers on Risky Hormuz Crossings
articles.description: Saudi Arabia’s shipping giant Bahri has been sending oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz in coordination with the U.S. military, Khalid Alhammad, president of Bahri Ship Management, said on Tuesday. Saudi Arabia, while boosting loadings and exports out of its Red Sea port of Yanbu, is also looking to raise shipments from within the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz. The Saudi firm is working at the government level with the United States to support Hormuz transits, Alhammad said at a Dubai event, as carried by Bloomberg.…

articles.title: Brent Crude Falls Below $90 for First Time Since August
articles.description: Brent Crude prices plunged to below $90 per barrel early on Tuesday, falling below that threshold for the first time since August, as U.S. President Donald Trump again signaled potential de-escalation in the Middle East and no need for strikes against Iran. As of early morning in Europe, the front-month Brent Crude futures had dropped to $89.70, and WTI Crude, the U.S. benchmark, traded below $85 per barrel, falling by over 2%. At the start of Asian trading, Brent Crude had dipped below $92 per barrel, following reports citing President Trump as…

articles.title: ADNOC Gas Posts Stunning Profit Recovery as Energy Exports Rebound
articles.description: ADNOC Gas doubled its net income to $1.34 billion for the third quarter from the previous quarter as it raised its domestic gas sales and LNG and sulfur exports. The gas arm of Abu Dhabi’s national energy company ADNOC on Tuesday reported strong performance across its domestic gas, LNG, export-traded liquids (ETL), and sulfur businesses. Net income jumped from $665 million for the second quarter to $1.34 billion for the third quarter, on core earnings, or EBITDA, soaring by 70% quarter-on-quarter to $2.03 billion. articles.title: LNG Traffic Through Hormuz Hits Highest Level Since Iran War Began
articles.description: Exports of liquefied natural gas via the Strait of Hormuz last month reached the highest total since February, at 31 tankers, compared with 27 in September, according to data from Kpler, as cited by Reuters. What is perhaps more impressive is that most of these cargoes were loaded from Qatar’s Ras Laffan hub, despite it still being under force majeure. In two cases, per Kpler, LNG cargoes loaded at Ras Laffan were then transferred to other tankers once the original vessels had cleared the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the increase in loadings,…

articles.title: Oil Prices Plunge Below $92 as Trump Signals Restraint on Iran
articles.description: Crude oil prices dropped to less than $92 per barrel for Brent and $86 for WTI following reports citing President Trump as not planning to attack Iran “at this point”. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $91.61 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was at $85.81 per barrel, after crashing by 7% on Monday, as reports emerged that the United States was open to letting Iran enrich uranium to almost 4% and Iran was, reportedly, going to accept the suggestion. The reports have not been confirmed by official sources from…

articles.title: The 75-Year Army Deal That Could Reshape America's Rare Earth Supply
articles.description: The U.S. Army has signed a non-binding term sheet with REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) to build the first-ever commercial rare earth processing operation on a U.S. military installation. The plan covers 200 acres at Tooele Army Depot in Utah, a lease that could run as long as 75 years, and provides first access for the Army to the rare earth products produced at this facility. Those metals are dysprosium and terbium. Every F-35, Tomahawk missile, and Virginia-class submarine depends on magnets made with them, and China produces nearly every ounce of both.…

articles.title: Oil Prices Sink on Iran Peace Hopes
articles.description: Oil prices plunged as renewed Iran peace hopes eased concerns over Middle East supply disruptions.

articles.title: Aramco Tower Targeted
articles.description: A Houthi attack damaged one of the landmarks of the Saudi Arabian capital's financial district.

articles.title: U.S. Traders Weigh the Cost of Taking Trump’s Russian Diesel
articles.description: Two tankers carrying Russian diesel have diverted from their intended American destinations, while another remains in the North Atlantic without a declared unloading port, complicating President Donald Trump’s agreement with Vladimir Putin to ease fuel prices. The Treasury has authorized Russian diesel transactions, but lawmakers warn that companies handling U.S. imports could still violate a congressional ban. The Russian tanker Talisman and Sierra Leone-flagged Leruo departed the Baltic port of Primorsk in October, initially declaring destinations…

articles.title: China to Spend $940B on Energy Transition in 2026
articles.description: China will once again be the biggest investor this year in alternative energy sources, spending some $940 billion on capacity and infrastructure. While still spending substantial sums on capacity, China will this year spend more on grid expansion and support infrastructure in a much-needed change of priorities. The figure above comes from the Global Energy Transition Report released this month by the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society, a state-linked think tank.
